display.title: The Baal Shem Tov Saved a Neshama, Part 1
display.summary_short: The Baal Shem Tov sends his attendant, Reb Yaakov, to travel and tell his stories. In Rome, before an eager rich listener, every story suddenly vanishes from his memory.
display.summary_long: The storyteller begins by explaining why the Baal Shem Tov came into the world: after terrible decrees left the Jewish people weak, like someone who has fainted, Hashem sent a neshama named Yisroel to wake them up. He first cared for their bodies, and then for their Torah and mitzvos, and he sent hidden tzaddikim to teach them. Before his passing, the Baal Shem Tov gives his attendant, Reb Yaakov, a mission: travel from town to town and tell the stories and teachings he witnessed. Years later his wife asks him to come home, and he answers that he will stop only when the Baal Shem Tov sends him a sign. The storyteller compares this to the Rebbe's answer that the Frierdiker Rebbe would still find a way to answer letters. Reb Yaakov then travels to Rome, to a wealthy community leader, Reb Moshe, who pays well for every Baal Shem Tov story. But at the Shabbos table, and at every meal after, Reb Yaakov cannot remember a single story, and people begin to whisper that he is a fake. As he is about to leave, one story comes back to him. To be continued.
display.lesson: A shliach keeps going until his Rebbe tells him he is done, and a Rebbe always finds a way to answer those who turn to him.
